items.prompt: Excuse me, do you know what time ___ today?

explanation.en: In an indirect question use statement order, with no do/does.
explanation.es: Tras Do you know… orden de afirmativa: the museum closes.

optionNotes.en: Correct: subject + verb after the question word.
Direct-question word order is not used inside an indirect question.
The verb must not come before the subject.

explanation.en: Who is the subject, so the verb follows directly with no did.
explanation.es: Si who es el sujeto, no se usa did.

optionNotes.en: Correct: question word as subject + past simple.
When who is the subject, there is no did; and after did the verb would be in the base form anyway, never chaired.
optionNotes.es: Si «who» es el sujeto no se usa did; y tras did nunca va el verbo en pasado.

optionNotes.en: Was chair is not a verb form that fits here.

items.prompt: I wonder ___ the exam results will be published.

explanation.en: I wonder introduces an indirect question, which keeps statement order.

optionNotes.en: Inversion (will the results) belongs to direct questions.
That cannot be placed before a question word.

items.prompt: Do you know if ___ to the party on Saturday?

optionNotes.en: Does cannot be followed by an -ing form.

items.prompt: Nobody could explain ___ the files had disappeared.

explanation.en: The clause after explain is not a question, so no inversion or auxiliary is needed.
explanation.es: Aquí no hay inversión: how the files had disappeared.

optionNotes.en: Had cannot come before the subject here.
Did cannot be added to the indirect clause.
